imprudent

/im-PROO-dent/ — stress on PROO · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

An action that is imprudent is unwise or careless, taken without properly thinking through the risks.

Diving into unknown water is imprudent, no matter how hot the day.

Example

He quit his job without lining up another position, a move his parents called imprudent.

Im (not) + prudent (careful, wise, thinking ahead). He did not think through the consequences or plan a safety net. Imprudent captures not just carelessness but a failure to foresee and plan for risks.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rash: Rash means acting in the heat of the moment, too quickly to think at all — the flaw is speed. An imprudent decision can be made slowly and calmly; what makes it imprudent is that the risks were never truly weighed. Every rash choice is quick; an imprudent one may be unhurried.

reckless: Reckless means seeing an obvious danger and plunging ahead anyway, often with a thrill in the risk. Imprudent is cooler and milder: a decision made without properly weighing its risks, no thrill required. A reckless driver races the train across the crossing; an imprudent one just skips the oil changes.

shortsighted: Shortsighted means grabbing today's benefit while ignoring tomorrow's cost — the flaw is a narrow time horizon. Imprudent is wider: any failure to weigh risks properly, whether they arrive next year or this afternoon. A shortsighted plan can feel safe for years; an imprudent one is careless about danger itself.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

prudent: careful and wise about consequences

cautious: deliberately careful to avoid risk

Where it sits · how badly the risks were ignored — hasty → unwise → careless → imprudent

hasty vs. imprudent: A hasty choice is simply made too quickly, but an imprudent choice ignores consequences that were plain to see.

unwise vs. imprudent: An unwise purchase costs you a little; an imprudent purchase gambles away things you cannot afford to lose.

careless vs. imprudent: A careless mistake comes from not paying attention, while an imprudent decision comes from refusing to weigh the risks at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — im-

Prefix — im-: not (the form in- takes before b, m, or p) (Latin)

Root — prudent

Root — prudent: careful, wise about the future (from Latin prudens, a contraction of providens, 'foreseeing') (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Im- (not) + prudent (careful, foreseeing) = not careful, failing to look ahead. Like impartial, this word carries its own antonym inside itself: prudent is exactly what the imprudent diver forgot to be.

Use the root in a new word: prudence

Use the root in a new word: prudence: With great prudence, she saved half of every paycheck before spending a cent.

Word Choice

formal

Reach for imprudent when someone has made a decision or taken an action without adequately considering the risks or consequences. The word emphasizes not just carelessness but a failure of foresight and judgment. It is common in advice, warnings, and discussions of financial or personal decisions.
